facts.statement: The genus Pampadromaeus was described by Cabreira et al. in 2011.
Pampadromaeus is known only from a single holotype specimen, ULBRA-PVT016, which is a partial but well-preserved skeleton.
facts.quote: Pampadromaeus is known only from the holotype specimen ULBRA-PVT016, a disarticulated, partial but well preserved skeleton from a single individual

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus lived during the early Late Triassic, approximately 230 to 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating to the Carnian faunal stage of the early Late Triassic, about 230–228 Ma ago

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus was a small, bipedal animal.
facts.quote: Pampadromaeus was a small bipedal animal.

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus exhibits a mosaic of both basal and derived traits.
facts.quote: It shows a mosaic of basal and derived traits.

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus had a much longer lower leg than thighbone, indicating it was adapted for running.
facts.quote: The lower leg was much longer than the thighbone, indicating a cursorial lifestyle.

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus had a total of eighty-eight teeth, with four in the premaxilla and about twenty in the maxilla and lower jaw.
facts.quote: There were four teeth in the premaxilla and about twenty in both the maxilla and the lower jaw for a total of eighty-eight.

facts.statement: A 2022 study found that Pampadromaeus lacked an invasive air sac system and its bones were not pneumatised.
facts.quote: In 2022, Tito Aureliano and colleagues performed a micro-computed tomography scan on the postcranial skeletons of some of the earliest saurischian dinosaurs that lived during the late Carnian including the herrerasaurid Gnathovorax with sauropodomorphs Pampadromaeus and Buriolestes, which showed that the invasive air sac system was absent and that their bones were not pneumatised.

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus was named by Sergio F. Cabreira, Cesar L. Schultz, Jonathas S. Bittencourt, Marina B. Soares, Daniel C. Fortier, Lúcio R. Silva, and Max C. Langer in 2011.
facts.quote: Pampadromaeus was first named by Sergio F. Cabreira, Cesar L. Schultz, Jonathas S. Bittencourt, Marina B. Soares, Daniel C. Fortier, Lúcio R. Silva and Max C. Langer in 2011

facts.statement: The generic name Pampadromaeus combines the Quechua word for 'plain' and the Greek word for 'runner'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Quechua pampa, "plain", in reference to the present landscape of the site, and Greek δρομεύς, dromeus, "runner", referring to the cursorial habits

facts.statement: The specific name barberenai honors the Brazilian paleontologist Mário Costa Barberena.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the Brazilian paleontologist Mário Costa Barberena.

facts.statement: Cladistic analyses have identified Pampadromaeus as a basal sauropodomorph.
facts.quote: Pampadromaeus was found to be a basal sauropodomorph in four different cladistic analyses.

facts.statement: Researchers note that the classification of Pampadromaeus as a basal sauropodomorph is not strongly supported due to difficulties in determining its affinities with early dinosaur groups.
facts.quote: The describers emphasized however, that this position was not strongly supported, showing the difficulties of determining the affinities of such early forms with the basal Dinosauromorpha, Saurischia, Sauropodomorpha and Theropoda.

facts.statement: Pampadromaeus is classified within the parent group Saturnaliidae.
Pampadromaeus belongs to the family Saturnaliidae.
Pampadromaeus is classified in the class Saurischia.
The time range for Pampadromaeus is the Carnian stage, from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (237 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Pampadromaeus is an extinct genus of basal sauropodomorph dinosaurs known from the Late Triassic (Carnian) Santa Maria Formation of the Paraná Basin in Rio Grande do Sul, southern Brazil.
